body:
This is not one experience, but my course through which I have used MDMA. I am writing this so that others will not suffer the same fate as I, although I know others have suffered much worse. Im just lucky enough to have stopped before it had an irreversible impact on my life. In this writing I will refer to MDMA as X since its shorter to type. Also previous information about includes that Ive used substances such as LSD, mushrooms, 2CE, and 25I, and cocaine. Note: none of these have ever become a problem for me including drinking or smoking for that matter.
To begin, it was when I was fourteen that I first started becoming interested in various types of drugs. My friends and I smoked and drank, and tried buying mushrooms at one point (we got ripped off). Shortly after starting smoking I had always wanted to try X, I heard about the wonderful effects of this drug and just had to try it for myself. Luckily, none of my friends were interested at that time so I gave up on this idea for a while.
Fast forward to last year, I had just entered college and tried X for the first time after being offered it by a floormate. During this experience I was too intoxicated to really recall any outstanding effects of it. Then when it was almost summer, I came into a readily available and trustworthy source for it. This is where the downfall began.
From May to August (2013), I used X approximately 20 times, starting from about once every two weeks and towards the end it starting to be around 1-2 times a week. I have never been an emotional person and lack empathy, so when I first started using this drug it allowed me to connect with my friends on a level I had never experienced before with roughly no crash in the following days. I LOVED IT, none of my friends judged me for it, most joined me in the use of it, and I had never been happier. In retrospect, I am aware that it would have been the happiest time of my life regardless, it was my first summer back from college in which I got to see all my old friends, we went on trips that never would have happened in high school, everyone seemed to be getting into EDM, and of course these were the people I had cared for and missed the most. At the end of summer when my friends were going back to college, I was on X and saying some goodbyes and it brought tears to my eyes. I realized how much I loved my friends and was so saddened to see them go. This wasnt in a bad way, the X allowed me to feel what I couldnt feel when I was sober Then it all went to hell.
Long story short, I came into some trouble and had to stop using completely including drinking and smoking. Once this happened I became aware of how attached I had become to this substance, I couldnt get it out of my head.
I became aware of how attached I had become to this substance, I couldnt get it out of my head.
Everything triggered memories of using it and being happy. Any party, any concert, and all of the music I listen to brings me back to times when I was rolling my face off. I have drank on the rare occasion since that time and every time I dont feel happy, I feel pissed off and agitated knowing that I could be rolling instead.
It has been a few months since I have been clean, yet I still spend the majority of time thinking about it. I know 20 times isnt an extraordinary amount, but it was enough to have me hooked. I dont know if it was the effects of X or if it was the trouble I got into, but I now suffer from mild panic attacks from time to time and have become paranoid to many things that I would have never been worried about before. I should also note that while mentally I have seen better days, my grades in school have improved dramatically and my relationships with my friends have all stayed the same or strengthened. No one judged me differently after I got clean and none of my friends abandoned me.
Overall I am glad that I got clean, I still truly miss the good old days, but for me they are over. I always think of where I would be right now if I wasnt forced to stop like the butterfly effect. I hope this helps some of you as for me it has been a struggle that is not close to being over. Please be safe about your use and dont be afraid to ask friends for help if you need it.
